conventions.convention: The regulator K is an independently specified finite-dimensional Lie group acting on the right on X; it is not identified with the full gauge group. The construction supplies no infinite-dimensional determinant or continuum functional measure.

The group density is positive and left invariant. R_x is the derivative at the identity of g ↦ x·g, M_x = dχ_x ∘ R_x, and Δ_FP is defined by M_x*λ = Δ_FP(x)ν, with ν = (μ_K)_e and λ the standard target density. Singular maps have Δ_FP = 0.
The orbit-to-slice density Jacobian at (e,s₀) is ρ_X(0,z₀)Δ_FP(s₀)/ρ_S(z₀). Equality with Δ_FP requires the stated target/slice density normalization.

The multiplicity formula assumes finitely many transverse zeros in the compact test-function support and distinct resulting slice points. The nonnegative approximate identity has compact support and unit integral; the result is a limit, including the empty zero set.
For a right principal bundle, fundamental vertical vectors are derivatives of p exp(tX), connection forms reproduce X, and R_h*ω = Ad_(h⁻¹)ω.

The global obstruction concerns every smooth SU(N) bundle over S³ or S⁴, N ≥ 2, under full AC. Smooth configuration and gauge spaces carry finite-atlas C∞ section topologies; orbit spaces carry quotient topologies. The reduced gauge group quotients by constant central sections Z_N.

Irreducibility means that based holonomy preserves no nonzero proper complex subspace of C^N; it does not require holonomy to equal SU(N). A continuous gauge representative means a continuous right inverse of the orbit projection.
The SO(2) example uses clockwise right rotation, so R_(x,y)(1) = (y,−x), M_(r,0)(1) = −r, and Δ_FP(r,0) = |r|.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC_ω, finite-dimensional regulated gauge-slice data specify 1 ≤ k ≤ n, a smooth right action of a k-dimensional Lie group K on an n-dimensional manifold X, positive densities, an embedded codimension-k slice defined locally by χ, and M_x = dχ_x ∘ R_x. Transversality at a slice point means M_x is an isomorphism; Δ_FP is its nonnegative density determinant.

For the stated finite-dimensional regulated data under AC_ω, invertibility of M_s₀ gives a local C¹ diffeomorphism Ψ:V×W→O, Ψ(g,s)=s·g. Its density Jacobian at (e,s₀) is ρ_X(0,z₀)Δ_FP(s₀)/ρ_S(z₀), and it gives the compactly supported Riemann change-of-variables formula. For relatively compact open Γ with x·closure(Γ) contained in U, a smooth compactly supported φ with exactly finitely many transverse zeros g_i of F_x in its support, distinct slice points x·g_i, and a nonnegative compactly supported smooth unit-integral approximate identity η_ε, the integral of φ(g)η_ε(F_x(g))Δ_FP(x·g) against μ_K tends to the sum of φ(g_i).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every smooth right principal SU(N)-bundle, N ≥ 2, over a nonempty compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary admits a smooth principal connection form satisfying vertical reproduction and right equivariance.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every smooth principal right SU(N)-bundle P over S^r, r ∈ {3,4} and N ≥ 2, with the stated smooth section and quotient topologies, neither the reduced irreducible orbit projection q_* nor the full smooth connection orbit projection q has a continuous section. The natural map from the reduced irreducible quotient identifies it with the open subset q(A^{∞,*}(P)) of the full quotient. Both conclusions hold for every bundle sector.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact AC_ω assumption inherited by the finite-dimensional gauge-data chain and used by the partition-of-unity supplier.
Full AC assumption in connection existence and the global obstruction; implication to countable choice.
Finite-dimensional real smooth group convention for the regulator and structure groups.
Left Maurer–Cartan convention in the local principal-potential transformation formula.
Full gauge group as base-fixing equivariant smooth bundle diffeomorphisms, without an asserted finite-dimensional Lie structure.
Adapted target coordinates, local orbit-to-slice coordinates, and inverse branches near transverse roots; the applications have positive dimension.
Compactly supported Riemann change of variables on the local diffeomorphism and on each transverse-root branch.
Support containment and sum-one conditions ensuring smooth zero extension and vertical reproduction in the glued connection.
A subordinate smooth partition for the finite trivializing cover, under countable choice supplied by full AC.
Ordinary product-chart convention underlying the cited principal-bundle section/retraction lemma.
The cited retraction argument: r ∘ i = identity implies r_*i_* = identity on based homotopy groups.

concerns.concern: The Definition says “in chosen bases it is |det M_x|” without specifying density-normalized bases. For arbitrary coordinate bases the determinant must be multiplied by the target density coefficient and divided by the source density coefficient. For example, M = identity with ν = 2|dt| and λ = |dy| has Δ_FP = 1/2. The defining density-ratio equation is correct, and the theorem's Proof 3.1 uses the correct normalization; clarify the basis qualification in this sentence.

seams_checked.note: The gauge-slice definition and connection-existence lemma preserve the supplied right-principal convention, vertical reproduction, adjoint equivariance, and local section-change formula. The independent finite regulator is explicitly distinguished from the full bundle gauge group.

Singer F2–F3 and Proof 2.1/4.1 use the actual C∞ section and quotient topologies, the smooth topological principal-bundle conclusion, and openness of the Sobolev irreducible locus. The sphere data meet the supplier's compact connected oriented boundaryless Riemannian and k > d/2 + 1 hypotheses.

Singer F4 and Proof 2.1 use exactly nonemptiness, path connectedness, and vanishing positive based homotopy groups for every sphere bundle in the supplier's scope. Holonomy irreducibility and the C∞ topology agree.

Singer F5–F6 and Proof 3.1 preserve the all-sector reduced smooth gauge-group claims: infinitely many components over S³ and nonzero fundamental group over S⁴. The section/retraction lemma is applied to a nonempty locally trivial principal topological bundle with weakly contractible total space. The associated diagrams have consistent objects, arrows, and compositions.

The formal-data definition and Slavnov–Taylor item use the finite-dimensional density determinant, including its zero value for singular maps and positivity/transversality equivalence at slice points. They explicitly retain the exclusions of continuum functional determinants, functional measures, and global gauge fixing.

The finite-orbit example directly computes its counterclockwise right-action derivative and unit-density determinant r, while distinguishing its positive local slice from the two-intersection global zero set. This differs consistently from the assigned clockwise example. Its orbit diagram matches the text; the Lorenz-gauge example makes no additional direct slice-theorem claim.
